newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-AUCKLAND OPEN NINE-POINT SUPER 12 LEAD.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-AUCKLAND OPEN NINE-POINT SUPER 12 LEAD.

text.p: Defending champions Auckland opened a nine-point lead at the top of the Super 12 rugby union table as last season's beaten finalists Natal were trounced 40-3 by lowly Queensland.

Auckland showed great character in overturning a 15-7 halftime deficit to beat the Otago Highlanders 45-28. They now have 40 points from nine matches, leading by nine from ACT and Wellington and by 13 from Natal.
Natal look to have lost their chance of a home semifinal after going down by six tries to nil in a desperately poor display against resurgent Queensland.
To compound their misery, dynmic winger Joos Joubert was sent off in the last minute for a high tackle on replacement wing Willie Carne.

Meanwhile, Wellington confirmed their status as the form team of the moment with a 19-3 defeat of New South Wales in Napier. The Hurricanes had a slow start to the season, but since the beginning of April they have been playing brilliant rugby.
All Black fullback Christian Cullen was again to the fore against the Waratahs, scoring a try started from inside his own 22 just three minutes into the game.

With ACT having the weekend off, Wellington's display propelled them to third place, behind the Australian side on points difference. The two meet in the final round of league games on May 18 in Canberra, with the winners likely to claim a home semifinal.
Elsewhere, early season frontrunners the Gauteng Lions (formerly Transvaal) continued their shocking away form with a 47-9 capitulation to Waikato in Hamilton.

In South Africa, bankruptcy-threatened Northern Transvaal pulled off a narrow 23-22 win over Canterbury Crusaders at Loftus Versfeld. Right-wing Casper Steyn tied up the match with a penalty from wide out in the dying minutes.

Canterbury, who finished bottom of the standings last year, are out of the running for a semifinal place now, but Northerns, together with Gauteng and Free State, can still qualify if Natal lose their last two games.
